precepts.text: Thus shall he do in the most strong holds with a strange god. That is the white man, starting with the Greeks all the way up to today. Here in our captivity we have stretched out our hands to their strange god that you think is Jesus. Whom he shall acknowledge and increase with glory. Robbed everything. And he shall cause them to rule over many. He caused his European allies to rule over many. And shall divide the land for gain. They divided the land of Israel and the land of Africa during the Berlin Conference for gain. That is what they did.
precepts.point: Arise for our help, and redeem us for thy mercies' sake.

note.label: The Waters of Noah Will Be Fire

precepts.why:
“Though thou hast sore broken us in the place of dragons, and covered us with the shadow of death.” The place of dragons is the seven heads: the great red dragon with seven heads and their lands, Greece, Rome, Spain, France, Germany, Russia and Great Britain, and the eighth head is America. Why has he covered us with the shadow of death? He has allowed these dragons to teach us lies, as a punishment for us disobeying his commandments. “If we have forgotten the name of our God, or stretched out our hands to a strange god”: see that part?

Daniel shows the strange god: “Thus shall he do in the most strong holds with a strange god, whom he shall acknowledge and increase with glory.” That is the white man, starting with the Greeks all the way up to today. Here in our captivity we have stretched out our hands to their strange god, the one you think is Jesus. He acknowledged him and increased him with glory, and robbed everything.

“and he shall cause them to rule over many, and shall divide the land for gain.” He caused his European allies to rule over many. They divided the land of Israel and the land of Africa at the Berlin Conference for gain. That's what they did.

So now we stretch out our hands to a strange god: white Jesus. Like the black woman in the video: Jesus is white, he's the white man, you look like Jesus, long hair, you are Jesus. We have stretched out our hands to a strange god and forgotten the name of our God. “They provoked him to jealousy with strange gods, with abominations provoked they him to anger.” White Jesus is a strange god; Allah is a strange god. “If ye forsake the Lord, and serve strange gods, then he will turn and do you hurt, and consume you, after that he hath done you good.” Have we not been hurt, in slavery, captivity, oppression and poverty? “There shall no strange god be in thee; neither shalt thou worship any strange god.” Yet we worship a god that doesn't look like us, act like us or talk like us, and want that strange god to bless us when he has done nothing but hurt us. Some of your mothers and fathers have that damn crucifix around their necks and on the walls of their houses.

“Envy thou not the oppressor, and choose none of his ways.” We have envied the oppressor and chosen his strange god and his strange religion. “Be not thou envious against evil men, neither desire to be with them.” We want into their politics, their religions, their schools; we want to look like them. The churches have done us a disservice. And the Lord knows it: “Shall not God search this out? for he knoweth the secrets of the heart.” We cry, “Awake, why sleepest thou, O Lord?”, and want him to intervene now, but he says, y'all have got to get yourselves together, men and women, and get right according to my word.

precepts.text: Our heart is not turned back, neither have our steps declined from thy way. That's how you got to be. That's how we have to be.
precepts.point: So this is where you self-examine: am I being a phony, a hypocrite amongst the brethren? Am I walking feignedly? Only you can answer that. You and God know the answer; we don't. If a sister ask us, what about this brother, we can only tell her what you show us. Is he really like that? You got to talk to this guy more in depth, more personally, to find out how they truly are. And some brothers can fake it real good.

note.label: Living Your Life As A Hireling

precepts.why:
Against the hireling who puts his hand to the plough and looks back, and the man who draws back, stands Israel's confession: “Our heart is not turned back, neither have our steps declined from thy way.” That's how you've got to be. That's how we have to be.

The heart that does not turn back and the steps that do not decline are what it means to walk before God unfeignedly. Those are the ones Ezra asks God to remember: “remember them, which according to thy will have known thy fear.”

So examine yourself. Has your heart turned back? Have your steps declined from his way since you first came in on fire? You and God know the answer.

precepts.text: As it is written, For thy sake we are killed all the day long; we are accounted as sheep for the slaughter. Paul is quoting Psalms 44:22: that is why he always said bring the books and the parchments, because his letters referenced things already written.
precepts.point: For the voice of him that reproacheth and blasphemeth; by reason of the enemy and avenger: at one time we knew the white man was our enemy. Now we see him as our avenger, our helper, our bosom buddy. A few decades ago he was your enemy; now he is your lover? It makes no sense.

note.label: Job Sees America's 250th Anniversary

precepts.why:
Paul writes: “As it is written, For thy sake we are killed all the day long; we are accounted as sheep for the slaughter.” That is prophecy right there. And where is it written? In this psalm: “Thou hast given us like sheep appointed for meat; and hast scattered us among the heathen”, and “Yea, for thy sake are we killed all the day long; we are counted as sheep for the slaughter.”

So when Paul was writing Romans 8:36, where do you think he got it? From Psalms. That is why he always said, bring the books and the parchments: the letters he was going to write would reference things already written in the Old Testament.

The sheep appointed for meat, scattered among the heathen, is Deuteronomy 28:64 fulfilled. God sold us for nought; he was not looking for financial gain when he allowed us to be sold. And Paul carried the same understanding into the New Testament: the people of God would be killed all the day long and counted as sheep for the slaughter. It did not stop with the apostles; it is still happening to our people today.

precepts.text: Then shall they deliver you up to be afflicted, and shall kill you: and ye shall be hated of all nations for my name's sake. A speaker in a clip shown in class admitted plainly that the whole world is anti-black; Christ said the same thing here first.
precepts.point: For the voice of him that reproacheth and blasphemeth; by reason of the enemy and avenger: at one time we knew the white man was our enemy. Now we see him as our avenger, our helper, our bosom buddy. A few decades ago he was your enemy; now he is your lover? It makes no sense.

note.label: Job Sees America's 250th Anniversary

precepts.why:
The psalm says, “Thou makest us a reproach to our neighbours, a scorn and a derision to them that are round about us. Thou makest us a byword among the heathen, a shaking of the head among the people.” Everybody hates us. They have nicknames for us. When we come around, they shake their heads: look at this, you want to move into the neighborhood here?

Christ said it first: “Then shall they deliver you up to be afflicted, and shall kill you: and ye shall be hated of all nations for my name's sake.”

In a clip shown in class, an Arab man said plainly that everybody is anti-black, not just the Arabs. Reflect back on this verse: he didn't lie. Christ said everybody is against us. Everybody.

That is the confusion the psalm speaks of. Our people go to school, get the education, talk like them, walk like them, wear the fake hair, and still get cast off, like the hundreds of thousands of black women with stable federal jobs dismissed in Trump's purge. We were not brought to this country to prosper and stay here. We were brought here to serve out our punishment, learn to repent of our sins, and then go back to greatness. Christians don't understand that.

precepts.text: When the laws are broken Israel is made a reproach to the neighbours, a scorn and a derision, a byword among the heathen, and a shaking of the head among the people; calling ourselves colors and bywords instead of our nationality is part of that estate.
precepts.point: Which shall hear all these statutes and say, surely this great nation is a wise and understanding people: they may not say it out loud today, but when they see Israel united in Christ and in order, that is what rises in their minds.

note.label: Deuteronomy 4: Neither Add nor Diminish

precepts.why:
The other side of the same coin. When the laws are broken: “Thou makest us a reproach to our neighbours, a scorn and a derision to them that are round about us. Thou makest us a byword among the heathen, a shaking of the head among the people.”

When Israel keeps the statutes the nations say “Surely this great nation is a wise and understanding people.” When Israel is fallen into sin the people look worse than the nations instead of wise and understanding: a reproach, a scorn and a derision, a byword among the heathen, a shaking of the head. Calling ourselves colors and bywords instead of our nationality is part of that estate.

Rulership belongs to the lineage only when the laws are kept. They may not say it out loud today, but when they see Israel united in Christ and in order, that is what rises in their minds.

precepts.text: We have heard with our ears, O God, our fathers have told us, what work thou didst in their days, in the times of old.
precepts.point: Paul advised the churches the same way his forefather Moses did: the things written aforetime, the Torah itself, were written for our learning. In Romans he quotes Moses over and over, including from this very chapter.

note.label: Deuteronomy 32: The Song of Moses, Prophecy of Israel's Fall and the Most High's Vengeance

precepts.why:
“ask thy father, and he will shew thee; thy elders, and they will tell thee.” The psalm shows it done: “We have heard with our ears, O God, our fathers have told us, what work thou didst in their days, in the times of old.” The knowledge of who we are and what the Most High did for us is passed down by the fathers telling it.

Before you learned this truth, did you know who you were before 1619? Somebody had to show you. The men teaching on the corners and bringing out these prophecies and breakdowns are the ones Moses said would teach you these things: ask thy father, and he will shew thee. Through them we have heard with our ears what work the Most High did in the times of old.

precepts.text: Remember the days of old; ask thy father and he will show thee, thy elders and they will tell thee.
precepts.point: When brothers ask "were you there?" or "how you know what color he was?" the answer is that the fathers heard and witnessed the Red Sea and the wars, and they told the following generations. We are supposed to search the scriptures.

note.label: Psalm 44: We Got Not the Land by Our Own Sword

precepts.why:
“We have heard with our ears, O God, our fathers have told us, what work thou didst in their days, in the times of old.” That is exactly what Moses commanded: “Remember the days of old, consider the years of many generations: ask thy father, and he will shew thee; thy elders, and they will tell thee.”

When brothers ask were you there, or how you know what color he was, the answer is that the fathers heard and witnessed the Red Sea and the wars, and they told the following generations. The fathers told how the Most High drove out the heathen with his hand and planted Israel, and that Israel “got not the land in possession by their own sword”, but by his right hand and “the light of thy countenance, because thou hadst a favour unto them.” We are supposed to search the scriptures, where the fathers and elders still tell it.

precepts.text: Remember the law of Moses for all Israel; Elijah is sent to turn the heart of the fathers to the children before the great and dreadful day.
precepts.point: When brothers ask "were you there?" or "how you know what color he was?" the answer is that the fathers heard and witnessed the Red Sea and the wars, and they told the following generations. We are supposed to search the scriptures.

note.label: Psalm 44: We Got Not the Land by Our Own Sword

precepts.why:
The fathers told us what the Most High did in the times of old, and Malachi tells us to hold on to it: “Remember ye the law of Moses my servant, which I commanded unto him in Horeb for all Israel, with the statutes and judgments.” The law is for all Israel. “Behold, I will send you Elijah the prophet before the coming of the great and dreadful day of the Lord”, and Elijah is sent to turn the heart of the fathers to the children before that great and dreadful day.

So the work the fathers told of, the heathen driven out and Israel planted by his right hand and not by our own sword, comes with the law of Moses to be remembered. When brothers ask how we know, this is the answer: remember what was told, and search the scriptures.

precepts.text: Things written before were written for our learning, sending us back to find the righteous path.
precepts.point: When brothers ask "were you there?" or "how you know what color he was?" the answer is that the fathers heard and witnessed the Red Sea and the wars, and they told the following generations. We are supposed to search the scriptures.

note.label: Psalm 44: We Got Not the Land by Our Own Sword

precepts.why:
“For whatsoever things were written aforetime were written for our learning, that we through patience and comfort of the scriptures might have hope.” What the fathers told, what the Most High did in the times of old, was written down for our learning. It sends us back to find the righteous path.

That is the answer to were you there and how you know what color he was: the fathers heard and witnessed the Red Sea and the wars and told the following generations, and it was written for us. We are supposed to search the scriptures, and through their patience and comfort we have hope.

precepts.text: Hearken diligently to His commandments and He sets thee on high and causes thine enemies to be smitten before thy face, fleeing seven ways.
precepts.point: Treading down the enemy through His name is not screaming a name you believe is the name of the Lord. The name means keeping the commandments.

note.label: Psalm 44: We Got Not the Land by Our Own Sword

precepts.why:
“Thou art my King, O God: command deliverances for Jacob. Through thee will we push down our enemies: through thy name will we tread them under that rise up against us.” Moses shows how the Most High commands that deliverance: “if thou shalt hearken diligently unto the voice of the Lord thy God, to observe and to do all his commandments which I command thee this day, that the Lord thy God will set thee on high above all nations of the earth”. Then: “The Lord shall cause thine enemies that rise up against thee to be smitten before thy face: they shall come out against thee one way, and flee before thee seven ways.”

Treading down the enemy through his name is not screaming a name you believe is the name of the Lord. The name means keeping the commandments: hearken diligently and observe to do them, and he sets thee on high and smites the enemies that rise up against thee, so they flee seven ways.

We cannot go it alone. Those who take up arms on their own without the Most High have their examples of failure; men who went to make a name for themselves fell. It is through him that we push down our enemies.

precepts.text: Salvation is that we should be saved from our enemies and from the hand of all that hate us.
precepts.point: In God they boast all the day long and praise His name forever. We are looking for that same salvation, which will be the destruction of our enemies.

note.label: Psalm 44: We Got Not the Land by Our Own Sword

precepts.why:
“But thou hast saved us from our enemies, and hast put them to shame that hated us.” That is what salvation is: “As he spake by the mouth of his holy prophets, which have been since the world began: That we should be saved from our enemies, and from the hand of all that hate us”.

David will not trust in his bow, nor will his sword save him; the Most High saved them from their enemies and put to shame those that hated them. “In God we boast all the day long, and praise thy name for ever.” We are looking for that same salvation, spoken by the holy prophets since the world began, and it will be the destruction of our enemies.

precepts.text: The Most High gave Jacob for a spoil because they would not walk in His ways nor obey His law.
precepts.point: He sold His people for nothing and did not increase His wealth by their price.

note.label: Psalm 44: We Got Not the Land by Our Own Sword

precepts.why:
“Thou makest us to turn back from the enemy: and they which hate us spoil for themselves. Thou hast given us like sheep appointed for meat; and hast scattered us among the heathen.” Isaiah asks who did it: “Who gave Jacob for a spoil, and Israel to the robbers? did not the Lord, he against whom we have sinned? for they would not walk in his ways, neither were they obedient unto his law.”

The enemy gained the power to spoil us because the Most High gave us over for our sins. He cast off, put us to shame and went not forth with our armies, not because the heathen were stronger, but because we would not walk in his ways nor obey his law.

precepts.text: If thou wilt not hearken, the curses come; thou shalt flee seven ways and be removed into all kingdoms of the earth.
precepts.point: He sold His people for nothing and did not increase His wealth by their price.

note.label: Psalm 44: We Got Not the Land by Our Own Sword

precepts.why:
“But thou hast cast off, and put us to shame; and goest not forth with our armies. Thou makest us to turn back from the enemy”. This is the curse Moses wrote: “if thou wilt not hearken unto the voice of the Lord thy God, to observe to do all his commandments and his statutes which I command thee this day; that all these curses shall come upon thee, and overtake thee”. Among them: “The Lord shall cause thee to be smitten before thine enemies: thou shalt go out one way against them, and flee seven ways before them: and shalt be removed into all the kingdoms of the earth.”

Turned back from the enemy, given like sheep appointed for meat, scattered among the heathen: that is being smitten before thine enemies, fleeing seven ways and being removed into all the kingdoms of the earth. He sold his people for nought because we would not hearken. The enemy's power to spoil us is the curse for our sins.

precepts.text: Thou shalt become an astonishment, a proverb, and a byword among all nations whither the Most High leads thee.
precepts.point: The shaking of the head is because we are an astonishment to our enemies. We went into slavery, our names were changed, our culture and lands were taken, and another nation took our name.

note.label: Psalm 44: We Got Not the Land by Our Own Sword

precepts.why:
“Thou makest us a byword among the heathen, a shaking of the head among the people.” That is the curse: “thou shalt become an astonishment, a proverb, and a byword, among all nations whither the Lord shall lead thee.”

The shaking of the head is because we are an astonishment to our enemies. We went into slavery, our names were changed, our culture and lands were taken, and another nation took our name. Israel became a reproach, a scorn, a derision, a byword, and a shaking of the head among the heathen the Most High led us to.

precepts.text: All that pass by clap their hands, hiss, and wag their head, asking is this the perfection of beauty, the joy of the whole earth.
precepts.point: The shaking of the head is because we are an astonishment to our enemies. We went into slavery, our names were changed, our culture and lands were taken, and another nation took our name.

note.label: Psalm 44: We Got Not the Land by Our Own Sword

precepts.why:
“Thou makest us a reproach to our neighbours, a scorn and a derision to them that are round about us.” Jeremiah saw it done: “All that pass by clap their hands at thee; they hiss and wag their head at the daughter of Jerusalem, saying, Is this the city that men call The perfection of beauty, The joy of the whole earth?”

The wagging of the head is the shaking of the head among the people. We were the perfection of beauty and the joy of the whole earth, and we became an astonishment: put into slavery, our names changed, our culture and lands taken, and another nation took our name. So the nations clap their hands and hiss and ask, is this them?

precepts.text: Righteousness belongs to the Most High but confusion of faces to all Israel scattered in the countries because they trespassed.
precepts.point: They will call us any name we want except Esau, as long as we keep celebrating Christmas, Thanksgiving, New Year's, the 4th of July, and birthdays. If they keep us in sin, the Most High will not fight our battles.

note.label: Psalm 44: We Got Not the Land by Our Own Sword

precepts.why:
“My confusion is continually before me, and the shame of my face hath covered me”. Daniel confesses the same thing for the whole nation: “O Lord, righteousness belongeth unto thee, but unto us confusion of faces, as at this day; to the men of Judah, and to the inhabitants of Jerusalem, and unto all Israel, that are near, and that are far off, through all the countries whither thou hast driven them, because of their trespass that they have trespassed against thee.” Righteousness belongs to the Most High, but confusion of faces to all Israel scattered through all the countries, because we trespassed.

When the enemy looks at us now, they no longer see a perfection of beauty. They see men sagging their pants, women dressed immodestly, whoredom in the songs, and they shake their heads. That is the confusion of faces, and it is because of our trespass.

precepts.text: As long as Israel sinned not, they prospered, but when they departed from His way they were spoiled and led captive.
precepts.point: They will call us any name we want except Esau, as long as we keep celebrating Christmas, Thanksgiving, New Year's, the 4th of July, and birthdays. If they keep us in sin, the Most High will not fight our battles.

note.label: Psalm 44: We Got Not the Land by Our Own Sword

precepts.why:
“For the voice of him that reproacheth and blasphemeth; by reason of the enemy and avenger.” The enemy was told exactly how it works with Israel: “whilst they sinned not before their God, they prospered, because the God that hateth iniquity was with them. But when they departed from the way which he appointed them, they were destroyed in many battles very sore, and were led captives into a land that was not their’s, and the temple of their God was cast to the ground, and their cities were taken by the enemies.” And the enemy's plan: “if there be any error against this people, and they sin against their God, let us consider that this shall be their ruin, and let us go up, and we shall overcome them.”

That is the enemy's play to this day. They will call us any name we want except Esau, as long as we keep celebrating Christmas, Thanksgiving, New Year's, the 4th of July, and birthdays. If they keep us in sin, the Most High will not fight our battles, and they know it: as long as Israel sinned not, they prospered, but when they departed from his way they were spoiled and led captive.

precepts.text: They that sit in darkness, bound in affliction and iron, because they rebelled against the word; He brought down their heart with labor.
precepts.point: This place is spiritual Egypt. The nations dealt wisely with us and put us to hard labor and bondage, and we are the essential workers on the front line.

note.label: Psalm 44: We Got Not the Land by Our Own Sword

precepts.why:
“Though thou hast sore broken us in the place of dragons, and covered us with the shadow of death.” Psalm 107 shows who sits in that shadow and why: “Such as sit in darkness and in the shadow of death, being bound in affliction and iron; Because they rebelled against the words of God, and contemned the counsel of the most High: Therefore he brought down their heart with labour; they fell down, and there was none to help.”

The broken part is that he brought down their heart with labour and there was none to help. Bound in affliction and iron, in hard labour, because we rebelled against the words of God. Yet the psalm says “yet have we not forgotten thee, neither have we dealt falsely in thy covenant”, and “Our heart is not turned back”; all this came, and still the heart is to hold to him.

precepts.text: The nation dealt wisely with Israel and made their lives bitter with hard bondage and service.
precepts.point: This place is spiritual Egypt. The nations dealt wisely with us and put us to hard labor and bondage, and we are the essential workers on the front line.

note.label: Psalm 44: We Got Not the Land by Our Own Sword

precepts.why:
“Though thou hast sore broken us in the place of dragons”. This place is spiritual Egypt. In Egypt they said, “Come on, let us deal wisely with them; lest they multiply”, and “they did set over them taskmasters to afflict them with their burdens.” “And the Egyptians made the children of Israel to serve with rigour: And they made their lives bitter with hard bondage, in morter, and in brick, and in all manner of service in the field”.

The nations have dealt wisely with us the same way and put us to hard labour and bondage; we are the essential workers on the front line. That is how the Most High brought down our heart with labour, sore broken in the place of dragons and covered with the shadow of death. But “the more they afflicted them, the more they multiplied and grew.”

precepts.text: A nation has not changed their gods, but Israel changed their glory for that which does not profit; is Israel a slave, why is he spoiled.
precepts.point: For His sake they are killed all the day long and counted as sheep for the slaughter. We changed our glory in Christ for that which does not profit.

note.label: Psalm 44: We Got Not the Land by Our Own Sword

precepts.why:
“If we have forgotten the name of our God, or stretched out our hands to a strange god; Shall not God search this out?” Jeremiah shows what Israel actually did: “Hath a nation changed their gods, which are yet no gods? but my people have changed their glory for that which doth not profit.” No other nation has changed their gods, yet Israel changed their glory. We changed our glory in Christ for that which does not profit.

Then comes the question that follows: “Is Israel a servant? is he a homeborn slave? why is he spoiled?” Israel was not born a slave, so why is he spoiled? Because we stretched out our hands to a strange god and changed our glory. And forgetting the name is not about the literal name; many run around saying this is the name, and it has not gotten them out of captivity.

precepts.text: Feed the flock of the slaughter, whose possessors slay them and hold themselves not guilty, saying blessed be the Lord for I am rich.
precepts.point: For His sake they are killed all the day long and counted as sheep for the slaughter. We changed our glory in Christ for that which does not profit.

note.label: Psalm 44: We Got Not the Land by Our Own Sword

precepts.why:
“Yea, for thy sake are we killed all the day long; we are counted as sheep for the slaughter.” Zechariah is told to “Feed the flock of the slaughter; Whose possessors slay them, and hold themselves not guilty: and they that sell them say, Blessed be the Lord; for I am rich: and their own shepherds pity them not.”

We are that flock of the slaughter. Our possessors slay us and hold themselves not guilty, those that sold us said blessed be the Lord, for I am rich, and our own shepherds pity us not. Counted as sheep for the slaughter, killed all the day long: that is Israel in captivity, and God, who knows the secrets of the heart, searches it out.

precepts.text: Your iniquities have separated between you and your God, and your sins have hid His face from you.
precepts.point: The face is hidden because of iniquity. Sins separate us from the Most High so that He will not hear.

note.label: Psalm 44: We Got Not the Land by Our Own Sword

precepts.why:
“Wherefore hidest thou thy face, and forgettest our affliction and our oppression?” Isaiah gives the reason the face is hidden: “But your iniquities have separated between you and your God, and your sins have hid his face from you, that he will not hear.”

The face is hidden because of iniquity. Sins separate us from the Most High so that he will not hear. That is why the soul is bowed down to the dust and the belly cleaves to the earth: we were once at a higher state and were brought low, and the way back to “Arise for our help, and redeem us for thy mercies’ sake” runs through putting away the sins that hid his face.

precepts.text: God hears not sinners, but if any man be a worshiper of God and does His will, him He hears.
precepts.point: The face is hidden because of iniquity. Sins separate us from the Most High so that He will not hear.

note.label: Psalm 44: We Got Not the Land by Our Own Sword

precepts.why:
“Awake, why sleepest thou, O Lord? arise, cast us not off for ever.” Why would the Most High seem asleep to our cry? “Now we know that God heareth not sinners: but if any man be a worshipper of God, and doeth his will, him he heareth.”

God hears not sinners. Our iniquities hid his face so that he will not hear; but if any man be a worshipper of God and does his will, him he hears. So the plea for him to arise for our help and redeem us is answered by doing his will, so that we are the ones he hears.

precepts.text: He will put the cup in the hand of them that afflicted thee, who said bow down that we may go over, and thou hast laid thy body as the ground.
precepts.point: The face is hidden because of iniquity. Sins separate us from the Most High so that He will not hear.

note.label: Psalm 44: We Got Not the Land by Our Own Sword

precepts.why:
“For our soul is bowed down to the dust: our belly cleaveth unto the earth.” Isaiah shows who made us bow: “But I will put it into the hand of them that afflict thee; which have said to thy soul, Bow down, that we may go over: and thou hast laid thy body as the ground, and as the street, to them that went over.”

They said to our soul, bow down that we may go over, and we laid our body as the ground and as the street for them to walk on. We were once at a higher state and were brought low. But the Most High will put the cup into the hand of them that afflicted us; that is him arising for our help and redeeming us for his mercies' sake.

moments.label: The Waters of Noah Will Be Fire

points: Though thou hast sore broken us in the place of dragons. That place of dragons are the seven heads. Remember the great red dragon with seven heads and their lands. You have got Greece, Rome, Spain, France, Germany, Russia and Great Britain, and the eighth head is America.
And covered us with the shadow of death. Why has he covered us with the shadow of death? He has allowed these dragons to teach us lies. Why? As a punishment for us disobeying his commandments.

note.label: The Waters of Noah Will Be Fire

points: If we have forgotten the name of our God, or stretched out our hands to a strange god. See that part right there? Or stretched out our hands to a strange god. So now we stretch out our hands to a strange god. White Jesus. Like we saw earlier with the black woman. Jesus is white, he is the white man, in fact you look like Jesus, long hair, you are Jesus. We have stretched out our hands to a strange god and we have forgotten the name of our God.

note.label: The Waters of Noah Will Be Fire

points: Shall not God search this out? for he knoweth the secrets of the heart.

note.label: The Waters of Noah Will Be Fire

points: Yea, for thy sake are we killed all the day long; we are counted as sheep for the slaughter. This is where Paul got it from. That was Romans 8:36. Paul did not just make things up and pull them out of the sky.

note.label: The Waters of Noah Will Be Fire

points: Awake, why sleepest thou, O Lord? arise, cast us not off for ever. Wherefore hidest thou thy face? You see that. We want the Lord to intervene now. But the Lord said, no, y'all have got to get yourselves together. You men, you women, get yourselves right according to my word.

note.label: The Waters of Noah Will Be Fire

points: And forgettest our affliction and our oppression? For our soul is bowed down to the dust: our belly cleaveth unto the earth.

note.label: The Waters of Noah Will Be Fire

points: Arise for our help, and redeem us for thy mercies' sake.

note.label: The Waters of Noah Will Be Fire

points: Thou hast given us like sheep appointed for meat; and hast scattered us among the heathen: that is Deuteronomy 28:64.

note.label: Job Sees America's 250th Anniversary

points: Thou sellest thy people for nought, and dost not increase thy wealth by their price: God was not looking for financial gain when he allowed us to be sold.

note.label: Job Sees America's 250th Anniversary

points: Thou makest us a reproach to our neighbours, a scorn and a derision to them that are round about us. Thou makest us a byword among the heathen: they have nicknames for us. A shaking of the head among the people: when we come around, they shake their heads.

note.label: Job Sees America's 250th Anniversary

points: My confusion is continually before me: this psalm is of the sons of Korah, who saw the vision of us going from the top nation down to the bottom, and could not reconcile what he was seeing. Bring it up to today: our people are confused. We get the education, we talk like them, walk like them, imitate them down to the hair, and we are still cast off. News read in class: black women with stable federal jobs were an easy target of the purge, with hundreds of thousands dismissed. Why? Because we were not brought to this country to prosper and stay here. We were brought here to serve out our punishment, learn to repent of our sins, and then go back to greatness. Christians do not understand that.

note.label: Job Sees America's 250th Anniversary

points: For the voice of him that reproacheth and blasphemeth; by reason of the enemy and avenger: at one time we knew the white man was our enemy. Now we see him as our avenger, our helper, our bosom buddy. A few decades ago he was your enemy; now he is your lover? It makes no sense.

note.label: Job Sees America's 250th Anniversary

points: The fathers told what work the Most High did in the times of old, driving out the heathen and planting Israel in the land.

When brothers ask "were you there?" or "how you know what color he was?" the answer is that the fathers heard and witnessed the Red Sea and the wars, and they told the following generations. We are supposed to search the scriptures.

note.label: Psalm 44: We Got Not the Land by Our Own Sword

points: Israel did not get the land by their own sword or their own arm, but by the right hand and the light of the countenance of the Most High, because He had favor toward them.

note.label: Psalm 44: We Got Not the Land by Our Own Sword

points: The Most High is called the king who commands deliverance for Jacob, and through Him the enemies are pushed down.
Treading down the enemy through His name is not screaming a name you believe is the name of the Lord. The name means keeping the commandments.

note.label: Psalm 44: We Got Not the Land by Our Own Sword

points: David will not trust in his bow, nor will his sword save him; the Most High saved them from their enemies and put to shame those that hate them.

note.label: Psalm 44: We Got Not the Land by Our Own Sword

points: In God they boast all the day long and praise His name forever. We are looking for that same salvation, which will be the destruction of our enemies.

note.label: Psalm 44: We Got Not the Land by Our Own Sword

points: Now the Most High has cast off and put them to shame, and goes not out with their armies; He makes them turn back and those that hate them spoil for themselves.

note.label: Psalm 44: We Got Not the Land by Our Own Sword

points: They are given like sheep appointed for meat and scattered among the heathen. The enemy gained the power to spoil us because the Most High gave us over for our sins.

note.label: Psalm 44: We Got Not the Land by Our Own Sword

points: He sold His people for nothing and did not increase His wealth by their price.

note.label: Psalm 44: We Got Not the Land by Our Own Sword

points: Israel became a reproach, a scorn, a derision, a byword, and a shaking of the head among the heathen.
The shaking of the head is because we are an astonishment to our enemies. We went into slavery, our names were changed, our culture and lands were taken, and another nation took our name.

note.label: Psalm 44: We Got Not the Land by Our Own Sword

points: Confusion is continually before them and the shame of their face covers them, because of the voice of him that reproaches and blasphemes.

note.label: Psalm 44: We Got Not the Land by Our Own Sword

points: All this has come, yet they claim they have not forgotten Him nor dealt falsely in His covenant, and their heart is not turned back.

note.label: Psalm 44: We Got Not the Land by Our Own Sword

points: Yet He has sore broken them in the place of dragons and covered them with the shadow of death. The broken part is that He brought down their heart with labor and there was none to help.

note.label: Psalm 44: We Got Not the Land by Our Own Sword

points: If they had forgotten the name of their God or stretched out their hands to a strange god, He would search it out, for He knows the secrets of the heart.
Forgetting the name again is not the literal name; many run around saying "this is the name" and it has not gotten them out of captivity.

note.label: Psalm 44: We Got Not the Land by Our Own Sword

points: For His sake they are killed all the day long and counted as sheep for the slaughter. We changed our glory in Christ for that which does not profit.

note.label: Psalm 44: We Got Not the Land by Our Own Sword

points: The plea is for the Most High to awake, arise, and not cast off forever, and to stop hiding His face and forgetting the affliction and oppression.

note.label: Psalm 44: We Got Not the Land by Our Own Sword

points: Their soul is bowed down to the dust and their belly cleaves to the earth; they were once at a higher state and were brought low.
